long_biography.plain_text:
Line 7's commercial expansion placed Marilyn Anne Horne within one of New Zealand's most visible apparel businesses. As co-owner with Ross Munro, she oversaw a company operating branded stores and a wider wholesale network across Australasia and other international markets.

The group widened its reach by acquiring Musto's Australian operation and supplying clothing beyond sailing to rowing, motor racing and rugby organisations. This broader strategy took Line 7 from specialist wet-weather gear into sportswear and casual clothing for men, women and children. The scale of its licensing and distribution network did not prevent financial pressure, and the company entered receivership in 2009 after more than two decades under Munro's ownership.

Identity therefore rests on the exact full name, New Zealand nationality and convergent business records, with confidence capped below very high.

Horne's co-ownership of Line 7 and later company holdings are documented. Self-made, operator and investor were considered but remain below the evidence threshold, so both classifications retain Unknown.

Line 7 entered receivership in 2009, and the current nature and materiality of Horne's Sportfolio and other holdings cannot be established. Fashion & Retail is therefore used only as the disclosed origin-sector fallback, not as a claim about present asset dominance.

No identity-secure personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or Personal Website was found. The current Line 7 website belongs to a later brand owner and is not proposed.

Apparel retail is assigned because Horne's ownership covered a substantial multi-market store, wholesale and distribution operation. America's Cup and Competitive sailing are excluded because Line 7's sponsorship and clothing-supply relationship does not make Horne a professional competitor, team owner or senior sailing-governance figure.
